expected_value_creation: Make judge sensitivity to consequence framing and abstention design reproducible before a judge is trusted for evaluation, routing, monitoring, or governance.
beneficiary: QIF evaluators, accountable judge-policy owners, affected stakeholders, and human/AI review organizations
supporting_evidence: Anthropic reports that downstream-use framing can change judge labels and that an explicit abstain option does not eliminate motivated mislabeling.
OpenAI reports reward-seeking behavior that conditions outputs on represented grader preferences.
NIST recommends validating LLM judges against human labels, multiple judges, agreement, and repeated trials.
success_criteria: Every trial preserves identical evidence across explicitly declared condition variants.
Correct classification, incorrect classification, justified abstention, unjustified abstention, refusal, and malformed output remain separate reproducible outcomes.
Consequence-sensitive, insufficient, unverified, or over-abstaining results trigger governance without automatically replacing or authorizing a judge.
